samples.summary: read-only `ensureSlidesRoot` no-op is NOT equivalent to `read()`'s in-memory backfill: `migrateDocument` never re-points `meta.themeId` at an existing theme, so a viewer can hit a thrown `getActiveTheme`
samples.evidence: `ensureSlidesRoot` now returns immediately on `options?.readOnly` (line 234). Its skipped backfill did two things `migrateDocument` does not: (a) it re-pointed `meta.themeId`/`meta.masterId` when the id was absent *or not present in the document's own `themes`/`masters` arrays* (yorkie-slides-store.ts:283-295, whose own comment says "pinning that id would make `getActiveTheme(doc)` throw at render time"), and (b) it seeded `layouts` with `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS` (line 251-253). `migrateDocument` (packages/slides/src/model/migrate.ts:79-87) only defaults `themeId` when it is *null* (`migrateMeta`, line 32) and sets `layouts = []` when the root has none — it does no cross-check against `themes`. So on a deck whose root carries `meta.themeId` (e.g. `'default-dark'`, which the seed branch writes when the creator was in dark mode) but whose `themes` array is missing/empty, a read-only mount reads `themes = [defaultLight]` with `meta.themeId = 'default-dark'`, and `getActiveTheme` (packages/slides/src/view/canvas/render-context.ts:88-95) throws `active theme '...' not found in document` at first paint — the viewer gets a crash rather than the "unmigrated deck rendered correctly" the comment promises. The missing `layouts` backfill separately degrades `resolveBackgroundFill`/`resolveBackgroundImage` (packages/slides/src/model/presentation.ts:215,231), which silently skip the layout level for a viewer while an editor sees it. The new test only covers a deck that already has `meta.themeId = 'default-light'`, so neither gap is exercised.

samples.summary: `shareTokenImageUploader` throws on failure, but the notes engine's `UploadImage` contract expects `null`-with-host-reporting; a share-link editor gets no error feedback when an image upload fails
samples.evidence: `uploadImage = shareTokenImageUploader(token)` returns `(file) => Promise<string>` that rejects on any failure (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:40-49 — `postShareTokenImage` throws). The engine documents `UploadImage` as "resolving with `null` means the host handled the failure itself" and treats a rejection as a last-resort fallback with only a `console.error` (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:19-24, 179-190). The owner route deliberately wraps its uploader in try/catch + `toast.error` and returns `null` (packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:208-231). The new shared layout passes the raw throwing uploader, so an anonymous editor-role visitor whose upload fails (413, network, unsupported type) sees the placeholder silently vanish with nothing in the UI.

samples.summary: Skipping `ensureAxisOrder` on a read-only mount drops the selection anchors, so a viewer's selection no longer survives a peer's row/column insert
samples.evidence: `ensureAxisOrder` now returns before growing the axis when `this.readOnly` (line 689). Its caller in the engine immediately checks coverage: `if (maxRow > rowOrder.length || maxCol > colOrder.length) { this.activeCellAnchor = null; this.rangeAnchors = []; ... }` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:3029-3044). Before this change a read-only mount grew the axis and therefore anchored; now any viewer selection past the persisted coverage clears the anchors, so `resolveAnchorsToRefs` leaves the visual selection unmoved when a peer inserts rows/columns above it and the highlighted cells no longer track the data they were on. Contained (display state only, no write), but it is a behavioural regression the guard introduces silently.

samples.summary: Read-only mounts now skip cross-sheet recalculation entirely with no display-only fallback, so a viewer can render stale cached formula values indefinitely
samples.evidence: `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` early-returns with only `this.worksheet.render()` when `this._readOnly`, and `sheet-view.tsx:1308/1322` additionally pass `needsRecalc = false` for a read-only mount. Unlike the slides path, there is no in-memory equivalent: `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` is the only thing that recomputes cross-sheet references, and it both computes and persists. So a viewer sees whatever cached value the CRDT happens to hold — which, for a sheet whose referenced tab changed but whose formula cells were never recalculated by an editor session, is a wrong number presented as current. The persisted-write concern is real, but the fix drops the read half with it.

samples.summary: `assertWritable` throws from `async` comment mutators whose callers do not catch, turning a read-only invocation into an unhandled promise rejection
samples.evidence: `YorkieStore.assertWritable` throws inside `addThread`/`addReply`/`editComment`/`deleteComment`/`setThreadResolved` (yorkie-store.ts:1307-1310 and call sites 1321/1347/1367/1375/1386). `handleCommentEdit` (sheet-view.tsx:965-970) and `handleCommentDelete` (972-977) simply `await storeRef.current?.editComment(...)` with no try/catch, and `handleCommentResolve` (936-963) likewise; these are passed straight to `CommentPopover` as `onEditComment`/`onDeleteComment`/`onResolve`. The new `readOnly` prop hides the affordances, so the path is currently unreachable through the UI — but the guard was deliberately made to throw for a future caller, and the nearest such caller produces an unhandled rejection rather than a visible failure.

samples.summary: The read-only Proxy neuters inherited `Object.prototype` methods too, so `String(store)` / a template literal on the handle throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`
samples.evidence: The `get` trap returns `noop` for any function that is not in `NOTE_STORE_READERS`/`HISTORY_METHODS`/`batch` (read-only.ts:151-160). That set is reached via the prototype chain as well, so `toString`, `valueOf`, `toJSON` and `hasOwnProperty` all become `() => undefined`. Combined with `getPrototypeOf: () => null`, ToPrimitive on the handle finds `Symbol.toPrimitive` undefined, then `toString()` → `undefined`, then `valueOf()` → `undefined`, and throws. Any diagnostic that interpolates the store (a log line, a Vitest failure message rendering the object, an error string) therefore throws instead of printing. `hasOwnProperty` returning `undefined` (falsy) is the same class of hazard. Mirrors the pre-existing docs wrapper, but the new file repeats it.

samples.summary: Divider drag divides by `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`, which is 0 when the container is exactly the divider's width, yielding `NaN` pane widths
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` then `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;`. With `track === 0` and the pointer exactly at `rect.left`, `ratio` is `NaN`; `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` is `NaN`, so both panes get `flex: 1 1 NaN%`. Only reachable in a pathologically narrow container (≤25px) in split mode, hence a nit — but the old `rect.width` denominator could not be zero the same way.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `ensureSlidesRoot` no-ops on readOnly (yorkie-slides-store.ts:234), skipping the themeId/masterId cross-check at :283-295 and the BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS seed at :251-253. Its claimed in-memory equivalent, `migrateDocument` (migrate.ts:77-93 with migrateMeta:32), only defaults `themeId` when nullish and defaults `themes` to `[defaultLight]` — it never re-points `themeId` at an existing theme, and defaults `layouts` to `[]`. `getActiveTheme` throws on mismatch (render-context.ts:88-97) and is called unconditionally in `drawSlide` (slide-renderer.ts:213), which the read-only share-link mount reaches (slides-view.tsx:198,285-288) with `store.read()` output (yorkie-slides-store.ts:470). The required root state (themes empty/missing + non-default themeId) is reachable through the public PUT /content path, whose validator accepts `themes: []` with any non-empty themeId (docs-content.controller.ts:534-547) and whose writer stores both verbatim (slides-tree.ts:97-105). The new test only covers themeId 'default-light' (tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:107-125). No guard elsewhere prevents the throw; a viewer crash on first paint is a correctness/critical-path defect in this lens.

finding.summary: Slides is the one collaborative surface left with an ungated load-time `doc.update()` on a read-only mount, so enforce-by-default wedges a viewer's sync
finding.evidence:
This change flips the auth webhook to enforcing by default (`isYorkieAuthEnforced`: anything but the literal `false` enforces) and, on that premise, gates every load-time/presence write on a read-only mount: `pdf-collab.tsx` (`initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}`, `onActivePageChange`), `yorkie-store.ts` (constructor presence, `updateSelection`, `ensureAxisOrder`), `yorkie-doc-store.ts` (`updateCursorPos`, `publishResolvedLocalCursor`), `board-view.tsx`, `slides-view.tsx` `broadcast()`, and `readOnlyNoteStore`.

Slides' *root* path is not gated. `slides-view.tsx:282` calls `ensureSlidesRoot(doc, …)` unconditionally inside the mount effect — with an in-tree comment that literally says "Known gap (intentional in this PR): `ensureSlidesRoot` may run a `doc.update()` migration block when a viewer mounts an unmigrated pre-v0.5 deck". `mobile-slides-view.tsx:147` does the same, and that is the component `shared-document.tsx:626` mounts for a phone-sized share-link visitor with `mode="view"`.

`ensureSlidesRoot` (`yorkie-slides-store.ts:218-298`) opens a `doc.update()` **unconditionally** at line 246 and writes `themes` / `masters` / `guides` / `meta.themeId` / `meta.masterId` / per-slide `notes` / text `data.blocks` whenever they are absent, plus a `needsRoot` branch at 228 that seeds `meta`/`slides`/`layouts`. `shared-document.tsx:983` passes `initialRoot={{}}` for slides for *both* roles, so nothing seeds the root for a viewer beforehand.

Consequence under the new default: a share-link `viewer` opening (a) a deck whose root was never seeded, or (b) any deck predating `guides`/`themes`/`masters`, emits a local change at load. The next `PushPull` therefore carries verb `rw` (`AccessAttributes(pack)`), `hasAccess` returns false for `link.role !== 'editor'`, and the webhook answers 403 — exactly the "wedging the viewer's own sync" failure the rest of the diff exists to prevent. The attach itself still succeeds (`READ_GATED_METHODS`), so the viewer sees the snaps

verdict.reason: The claimed ungated call does not exist. `ensureSlidesRoot` takes a `readOnly` option and returns immediately at yorkie-slides-store.ts:234 — before `doc.getRoot()` and before both `doc.update()` blocks (the `needsRoot` seed at 241-255 and the themes/masters/guides/meta/notes/blocks backfill at 259-311). Both call sites pass it: slides-view.tsx:287 passes `readOnly: readOnlyMount` (`readOnly === true`, line 198) and mobile-slides-view.tsx:154 passes `readOnly: mode === "view"`. The share-link viewer reaches those gated paths in both form factors: shared-document.tsx:411 derives `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` and forwards it as `readOnly={readOnly}` to SlidesView (:503) and `mode={readOnly ? "view" : "edit"}` to MobileSlidesView (:626-627). The "Known gap (intentional in this PR)" comment the finding quotes as in-tree evidence is not in slides-view.tsx — a tree-wide grep for "Known gap" matches only docs/ files. Tests at tests/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.test.ts:79-131 cover the read-only no-op. `initialRoot={{}}` at shared-document.tsx:983 is real, but with the gate present no local change is emitted at viewer load, so no `rw` PushPull and no 403 wedge.

finding.summary: Read-only sheet mount still writes the CRDT root through the cross-sheet recalc path, which the new `readOnly` gate does not cover
finding.evidence: The new constructor comment claims `readOnly` silences "the three writes the grid makes without the user ever running an editing command" (yorkie-store.ts:82-93), but `runRemoteSync(true)` at sheet-view.tsx:1300 runs unconditionally on mount (and again from the remote-change subscription at sheet-view.tsx:1312) for a read-only viewer. It calls `sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()` → `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:2943-2981), which opens `store.beginBatch()` and runs `calculate(...)`. `calculate` writes cells via `sheet.setCell`/`deleteCell` — unconditionally for spill results (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:118-141) and for cycled cells (line 67) — and `recomputeFilterHiddenRows()` (sheet.ts:2976) writes hidden state. `YorkieStore.endBatch()` then issues a real `doc.update()` (yorkie-store.ts:1176-1187) because `readOnly` is not consulted there or in `set`/`setHiddenState`. So a share-link viewer opening a sheet containing a spilling or cross-sheet formula (or a cycled formula) still performs the `rw` PushPull the PR is trying to eliminate — the viewer's sync wedges exactly as before, and if the webhook were permissive the viewer would be mutating the owner's document.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. The initial sync call site is `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` (sheet-view.tsx:1308), not `runRemoteSync(true)`, so a read-only mount takes the `sheet.render()` branch (sheet-view.tsx:1185-1189) and never calls `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas()`. The remote-change subscription likewise passes `readOnly ? false : needsRecalc(ops)` (sheet-view.tsx:1322), not an unconditional recalc. Additionally, the engine method itself is gated: `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` returns after a plain render when `this._readOnly` (spreadsheet.ts:971-977), and `_readOnly` is set from the mount options passed at sheet-view.tsx:1014-1017 (spreadsheet.ts:78). So neither call site nor the engine reaches `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (sheet.ts:2943) / `store.beginBatch()` / `calculate()` for a read-only viewer, and the described CRDT write path does not exist.
